title: Scoring a Touchdown with Variable Pricing: Evidence from a Quasi-Experiment in the NFL Ticket Markets
eligible_reason: Staggered binary adoption exists (15 teams adopt variable pricing in 2014, 3 in 2015, 14 never), but every reported regression includes time-varying team-season/game controls (datp1, sb_pres_odd, sb_week_odd, net_movement), the main columns use propensity-score weights (IPW) and add the continuous interaction vp_datp1 as an additional treatment regressor. The only control-free DiD is a 2x2 regression without fixed effects quoted in the Section 4.1 prose.
design_notes: Inferred from Codes/PrimaryMarketTables.do, SecondaryMarketTables.do and the data. Unit: home team (ts / t_short); time: NFL season (year, 2012-2015) with game-week FE (nflweek) and opponent FE (os); observation = home game. Treatment vp = 1 for teams on variable pricing (treated1: switched 2014; treated2: cle, den, nyj switched 2015). Table 3: reg capa_util vp [vp_datp1] atp12 datp1 sb_pres_odd sb_week_odd ln_g_inc_demean ln_g_eth_demean med_inc_demean pop_mil_demean net_movement i.nflweek i.year i.os i.ts, sample year 2012-2015, non-international games, excluding sfo, min, ten; cols 1-2 [pweight=psweight10a], cols 3-4 unweighted; robust SEs. Table 9 / Figure 2: relative-season dummies (vp_23, vp_2, vp1, vp2) with the same controls and weights. Secondary-market tables use daily resale prices with similar controls. Table 6 adds tobit and Poisson.
estimators_reported: TWFE static with IPW (reg with i.ts i.year i.nflweek i.os)

ineligible_specs.reason: time-varying controls (datp1, sb_pres_odd, sb_week_odd, net_movement); cols 1-2 IPW weights; cols 2,4 add vp_datp1
same controls plus IPW and additional treatment interactions
relative-time dummies with time-varying controls, IPW, vp_datp1

screener_notes: Near-miss: Table 3 col (3) is unweighted TWFE with team, season, week and opponent FE, but with time-varying controls in every column; dropping them would be a new specification, not a replication of a reported one. Only two adoption cohorts (2014, 2015). Abstract reports the 1.59% effect from the IPW specification.
